justifications.c1: Only all-cause insurer aggregates (NFU Mutual farm-fire claims £102m in 2024, £48m earlier) and incident sizes with no £ amount (800 t hay, 1,700 t straw); the share due to self-heating and a per-claim £ figure were not found.
justifications.c2: Fire-service and extension guidance sets daily checks from 65°C and every four hours from 70°C (Dorset & Wiltshire FRS via Agriland, search-confirmed; CFA, Alberta, Kentucky), but only during a 2–6-week post-baling window each season, and fires per farm are rare.
justifications.c3: Manual probing with pipe and thermometer is documented by fire services, and paid moisture testers and preservative applicators exist, but no labour time or cost of probing was found.
justifications.c4: No regulation or UK policy condition requires probing (recorded not found); insurers are engaged: Cornish Mutual piloted Haytech with 10 member farms (search-confirmed) and Nationwide (US) discounts Haytech, but no UK subsidy or claim refusal is evidenced.
justifications.c5: The buyer is 'farmers and barn owners' with no job title or budget evidence; insurers are a possible payer but only via a 10-farm UK pilot and a US discount.
justifications.c6: Insurer programmes already bundle comparable monitoring for this exact niche: Cornish Mutual's Haytech trial and loss-prevention page (UK, search-confirmed) and the Nationwide partnership (US, search-confirmed); baler-sensor dealers (Harvest Tec, Carr's Billington) also reach the same farmers. Scale of the UK programme is unproven.
justifications.c7: Willingness to pay is proven (Haytech $99/month for 100 probes via Nationwide, AU products at $385–$660), but the incumbent already holds the UK and US insurer channels; the claimed gap (Haytech's 2G GPRS kit) has no complaint or switch-off evidence.
justifications.c8: Comparable probes exist (Haytech 40 cm spike with up to 5-year battery, FAIE 177 cm lance), but no component prices or BOM were gathered, and probe robustness and radio range in stacks and steel barns are unevidenced.
justifications.c9: Comparable products charge subscriptions (Haytech $99/month via Nationwide, a year of service in the Gallop kit), but value is seasonal and there is no statutory or insurer record-retention duty.
justifications.c10: Insurer loss data (NFU Mutual), fire-service incident records and press releases (Devon & Somerset, Cumbria, Mid and West Wales) and trade/local press; no first-hand forum complaints were found.

weakest: Quanturi Haytech already occupies the insurer channel the idea would rely on (Cornish Mutual in the UK, Nationwide in the US), and there is no per-incident £ figure or compliance duty to differentiate on.
